title: Tulip Mania: The Flower That Fooled History
thesis: Tulip mania was real for a few traders; the ruin of a nation is a legend built on a satire and a Victorian bestseller.

loops.question: How did a flower become a fortune, then nothing?

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.purpose: Open on the Haarlem auction without buyers; contrast with the 10,000-guilder peak; open the central loop.
chapters.exit_hook: How does a flower become a fortune, then nothing at all?

chapters.title: The Rise
chapters.purpose: From Clusius's garden to tavern contracts; Mackay's picture of a whole nation trading.
chapters.exit_hook: Everyone, it seemed, was about to get rich.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.purpose: The collapse, the guild ruling, and the twist: the ruin Mackay described is contested by Goldgar's archival study.
chapters.exit_hook: The bubble was real for a few; the legend was written for everyone else.

callback_plan: The auction without buyers (CH1) returns as the collapse in CH3
next_video_bridge: The South Sea Bubble: when a whole kingdom really did go broke.
